I am planning a vegetable garden on a 6 m by 4 m plot that gets about seven hours of direct sun in summer and three in winter. The soil is heavy clay with a pH of 6.8; last spring I dug in 40 litres of compost and 10 kg of grit, and drainage improved, but the beds still puddle for a day after heavy rain. I want to grow tomatoes, runner beans, courgettes, garlic and salad leaves, and I can spend about five hours a week on it. Last year my tomatoes split after a dry fortnight followed by a storm, the courgettes cropped well until mildew arrived in late August, and slugs ate most of the lettuce seedlings within a week of planting out. I have two 200-litre water butts, a cold frame and a small greenhouse that reaches 35°C on sunny afternoons, and a 3-year-old compost heap that is mostly grass clippings and smells sour by midsummer. Which crops should go where, should I build raised beds 30 cm deep or keep improving the clay, how often and how deeply should I water during a heatwave, and what would you change about last year's timing? Answer briefly, listing the main risks.
